description:
# ErrorMessage coverage implementation plan

## Scope and verified baseline

Planning-only handoff for the coordinator to merge before implementation. Production target: `lib/zaq/agent/error_message.ex`; supplied coverage: 81%; supplied uncovered lines: **61, 150, 155, 181, 182, 183, 193, 198, 210, 211, 216, 236, 270, 274, 284, 288**. These are current one-based source lines; several identify a clause head rather than its executable return expression. Coverage must be assessed against the complete module, not just these sixteen locations.

Serena initial instructions, source overview/body, and existing test overview/body were successfully inspected. Targeted numbered reads confirmed the line mapping. Context Mode failed with `disk I/O error`; bounded native reads/searches supplied the remaining evidence. Policies consulted: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agent-tools.md`, `docs/testing-approach.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md` planning/validation sections, `docs/services/agent.md` public error contract and harness-critical checks, and `docs/services/system-config.md` credential provenance/secret lifetime requirements. `test-coverage-planner` was loaded. `bw prime` was the required orientation command; no tracking or Git mutations, tests, or application commands were performed.

**Action reuse assessment: N/A — tests only; no operations changed.**

The real implementation is a pure translation boundary. It reads no runtime configuration, database, clock, process state, or external provider. Build ReqLLM exception structs as input values; invoking providers, credential resolution, Factory, Executor, or NodeRouter would add irrelevant boundaries.

## Exact file ownership and implementation sequence

**Only test implementation owner:** `test/zaq/agent/error_message_test.exs`, module `Zaq.Agent.ErrorMessageTest`.

Keep its existing `use ExUnit.Case, async: true`, `use ExUnitProperties`, `alias Zaq.Agent.ErrorMessage`, constants, and assertions. Add examples to its existing `from_reason/2`, `recovery_for/1`, and `public_reason_for/1` describes; add a dedicated `with_credential_owner/2` describe for wrapper/provenance tests and properties. No new shared support module or second property test file is needed.

Implementation order: (1) merge/deduplicate this plan with coordinator plans; (2) add deterministic examples A–G below; (3) add the focused properties; (4) coordinator performs isolated validation and fresh whole-module coverage assessment. All work stays in the authorized dirty tree. Preserve existing `test/e2e/*` and `test/zaq_web/people_browser_test.exs` edits. No production changes, public test hooks, coverage exclusions, new mocks, or modified test bootstrap.

Existing coverage to reuse rather than reproduce: prompt guards, primary context-window variants, persistence message variants, budget messages/types, personal credential messages, direct 401 owner enrichment, credential recovery, and unknown-reason fallback properties. Missing tests concern distinct public methods or branch behavior even when the same exception fixture appears elsewhere.

## Deterministic scenario specifications

Use explicit expected literals below, never a call back into ErrorMessage to calculate an expected value. Table rows may be separate named tests or a compact table in one focused test; failures must identify the input row.

### A. Generic context-window reason — line 61

Extend the existing context-window message test with `{:context_window_exceeded, :unknown_limit_reason}` and fallback `"fallback must not win"`. Assert exactly:

> This request exceeds the selected model's context window. Shorten the request or adjust the agent configuration before trying again.

Also send `{:request_transformer, {:context_window_exceeded, :unknown_limit_reason}}` through `from_reason/2` with the same fallback and assert that same literal. This verifies generic reason handling and public transformer delegation; the existing mandatory-payload and no-input-budget examples cannot hit line 61.

### B. Recovery status boundaries and wrapper propagation — lines 150, 155

Add `"classifies provider recovery without inferring credential ownership"` under `recovery_for/1`:

| Input struct | Status values | Exact recovery | retryable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `%ReqLLM.Error.API.Response{}` | 500, 503, 599 | `:retry` | `true` |
| `%ReqLLM.Error.API.Response{}` | 499, 429, 401, nil, `"503"` | `nil` | `false` |
| `%ReqLLM.Error.API.Request{}` | 429, 500, 503 | `:retry` | `true` |
| `%ReqLLM.Error.API.Request{}` | 428, 430, 499, 401, 403, nil, `"500"` | `nil` | `false` |

Set only `status` for these fixtures. Response 429 intentionally differs from Request 429: the implementation only retries response errors with integer status >=500. Do not change that behavior to make the table symmetrical. These are error structs, not outbound requests.

Add `"propagates recovery through failure wrappers"`: for each of Request 503 (expected `:retry`) and Request 401 without provenance (expected `nil`), exercise a failed tuple, a Stream cause, and `{:failed, :error, {:request_transformer, %ReqLLM.Error.API.Stream{cause: inner}}}`. Assert the explicit expected recovery and boolean for every wrapper. The failed tuple enters line 155; the nested example also protects the neighboring transformer/stream delegates. A raw authentication status must not imply personal recovery.

### C. Trusted ownership and wrapper preservation — lines 181–183

Add a dedicated `with_credential_owner/2` describe. Construct the inner Request with explicit `reason: "synthetic-secret-detail"`, `response_body: %{"secret" => "synthetic-provider-secret"}`, and the specified status. All strings are synthetic; no credentials are loaded.

1. **Changed branch, line 183:** wrap Request status 401 and 403 as `{:failed, :error, inner}`; exercise both owners `"person"` and `"org"`. Assert exact equality to `%{reason: :provider_authentication_failed, owner_type: owner}`. Equality of the entire map proves wrapper removal and absence of body, exception, and secret fields. Assert `public_reason_for(result) == :provider_authentication_failed`; personal recovery is `:personal_credentials`, org recovery is `:contact_administrator`; retryable is false.
2. **Unchanged branch, line 182:** failed-wrapped Request 429 with owner `"person"` returns the entire original wrapper using `===`. Also failed-wrapped Request 401 with owner `nil` returns exactly the original wrapper. Add explicit invalid-owner values `"unknown"`, `:person`, and `""` to confirm only trusted string values enrich. These rows fail opposite guards and protect the distinction between selected ownership and provider status.
3. **Recursion through both wrapper types:** Request 403 inside `{:failed, :error, %ReqLLM.Error.API.Stream{cause: inner}}` enriches for `"person"`; `%ReqLLM.Error.API.Stream{cause: {:failed, :error, inner}}` enriches for `"org"`. For the same shapes with Request 500, return the original complete structure using `===`. This also exercises the neighboring Stream changed/unchanged arms without reaching into private functions.

Both case arms are necessary: an enrichment-only test would leave line 182 unproven. Original wrappers retaining a provider payload are internal values, not public DTOs; only the enriched result must discard that payload at this method boundary.

### D. Budget precedence in public metadata — lines 193, 198

Add `"normalizes both budget body shapes before status classification"` under `public_reason_for/1`:

- Nested: `%ReqLLM.Error.API.Request{status: 401, response_body: %{"error" => %{"type" => "budget_exceeded", "detail" => "synthetic-secret"}}}` → exactly `:budget_exceeded` (line 193).
- Flat: `%ReqLLM.Error.API.Request{status: 429, response_body: %{"type" => "budget_exceeded", "detail" => "synthetic-secret"}}` → exactly `:budget_exceeded` (line 198).

The conflicting status values demonstrate precedence over authentication/rate-limit classification. Existing `from_reason` and `error_type_for` budget tests do not execute these public metadata clauses.

### E. Remaining metadata mappings — lines 210, 211, 216

Add `"normalizes non-budget provider failures to safe public atoms"`:

- Request status 400, 422, 499, and nil, with `reason: "synthetic-secret"` and non-budget body `%{"detail" => "synthetic-secret"}` → exactly `:provider_request_rejected` (line 210).
- Response status 200 and 503 with synthetic reason → exactly `:provider_response_failed` (line 211). A Response 503 has retry recovery but remains this metadata category; do not assert `:provider_unavailable` for it.
- Request 500 and 503 → exactly `:provider_unavailable` as a boundary contrast to Request 499.

Add `"reduces persistence failure details to a safe public reason"`: each of `{:persist_failed, :trace_artifact_too_large}`, `{:persist_failed, :db_down}`, and `{:persist_failed, %{detail: "synthetic-secret"}}` → exactly `:persist_failed` (line 216).

Check Stream and request-transformer wrappers around Request 422 against the same explicit `:provider_request_rejected` atom. Existing failed-tuple metadata coverage can remain as-is.

### F. Non-person credential guidance — lines 236, 270, 274

Add `"uses non-person guidance without trusted personal ownership"` under `from_reason/2`. For each row below, construct a reason map first with `owner_type: "org"`, then with the owner key omitted, then with `owner_type: nil`. Include `credential_id: 42` and `provider_body: "synthetic-secret"` to ensure payload extras cannot change the output. Pass fallback `"fallback must not win"`.

| Reason | Line | Exact message | Recovery | retryable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `:credential_refresh_busy` | 236 | `The AI credentials are being refreshed. Please try again shortly.` | `:retry` | `true` |
| `:credential_unavailable` | 270 | `The configured AI credentials are invalid or unavailable. Ask an administrator to update them.` | `:contact_administrator` | `false` |
| `:credential_refresh_failed` | 274 | `The configured AI credentials could not be refreshed. Ask an administrator to reconnect them.` | `:contact_administrator` | `false` |

Assert the full message, recovery and retryable boolean; `public_reason_for/1` and `error_type_for/1` must return the row's reason atom. Explicit message equality protects omission of secret details and People-portal instructions. Existing personal-owner examples remain the contrasting branch; missing ownership is not permission to assume personal identity.

### G. Neutral provider message status classes — lines 284, 288

Add `"gives neutral guidance for unowned provider authentication errors"`: direct Request 401 and 403, and Response 401, with synthetic exception detail, passed to `from_reason/2` with an unrelated fallback, must equal:

> The AI provider rejected the credentials used for this request. Update the credentials or ask an administrator for help.

This calls the private helper through the public API (line 284); calling with an already-enriched credential map does not reach it. For each raw error assert recovery nil and retryable false.

Add `"distinguishes ordinary client errors from special provider statuses"`: Request 400, 422, 499 and Response 422 must equal:

> The AI provider rejected the request. Check the request or ask an administrator for help.

These enter line 288. Boundary contrast: Request 399 → `There was an error communicating with the AI provider. Please try again.`; Request 500 → `The AI service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.`. Existing 429 tests retain their rate-limit expectation. Use synthetic reason/body values; messages must be the expected constant regardless of those details.

## Focused property coverage

Use the existing ExUnitProperties/StreamData imports and module. Keep generators bounded; use no dynamic atom creation or unconstrained exception generation. Properties supplement the deterministic line-driving examples, so no line's coverage depends on random selection.

1. **Trusted wrapped authentication discards arbitrary payloads.** Generate status from `[401, 403]`, owner from `["person", "org"]`, and alphanumeric payload length 1–64. Put `"__secret_#{payload}__"` in Request reason and response_body. Generate a list of wrapper tags from `[:failed, :stream]`, length 1–4, then reduce it around that Request. Assert enrichment equals exactly the two-key authentication-failure map. Assert public reason and independently selected recovery, and refute retryable. This covers arbitrary payloads and recursion combinations while proving the secret-removal invariant.
2. **Absent or invalid provenance never enriches wrappers.** Generate owner from `[nil, "", "unknown", :person]`, authentication status from `[401, 403]`, payload as above, and wrapper tags length 1–4. Assert `with_credential_owner(wrapped, owner) === wrapped`, recovery nil, and retryable false. These guards are a security-default boundary and justify property testing even though production is unchanged.
3. **Non-person credential guidance ignores arbitrary extra details.** Generate one of the three reason/expected-message/recovery/boolean tuples in F, owner shape from `[:absent, nil, "org", "unknown", :person]`, and payload length 1–64. Explicitly omit the key for `:absent`; other values are literal map values. Assert exact tuple-supplied message, recovery, boolean, and reason atom. This tests safety over payloads and malformed ownership, not a reproduction of production branching logic. Keep the existing personal-payload property intact.

## Helpers, mocks, and isolation contracts

- Reuse existing ExUnit setup, alias and StreamData capability. Existing tests use inline ReqLLM structs and define no fixture helpers; nearby `test/support/` search found no ErrorMessage/ReqLLM-specific reusable builder.
- A single private **test-file-local** helper `wrap_reason(reason, tags)` is justified by repeated property composition: `:failed` produces `{:failed, :error, inner}`, `:stream` produces `%ReqLLM.Error.API.Stream{cause: inner}`. Define reduction order clearly (left fold: last tag is outermost). It creates input values only and never calculates expected results. Deterministic tests should keep wrapper inputs visible.
- Keep simple Request/Response construction inline. No generalized fixture factory, shared setup, additional support file, mocks, Mox contracts, provider HTTP stubs, NodeRouter stubs, TestConfig overrides, or runtime credential fixtures.
- All scenarios stay `async: true`: no application environment changes, global Mox mode, SQL checkout/shared sandbox, shared files, ETS, registered processes, or network access. No serial module is needed.
- The synchronous return value is the observation/completion signal. No sleeps, polling, messages, monitors or process lifecycle synchronization are required.
- The repository's `test/test_helper.exs` and Mix test alias still start the normal application/test infrastructure; pure unit scenarios do not imply that the repository command can run without its configured test database. Do not bypass bootstrap or add test-only startup changes.

## Reachability and contract caveats

**None of the sixteen supplied lines is unreachable.** The mapping above reaches every clause through an exported API. Lines 182 and 183 are mutually exclusive in a single call but reachable via unchanged and enriched inner reasons respectively. Credential and provider private helper clauses are publicly reachable; exposing them is unnecessary.

Potential false assumptions to avoid:

- ReqLLM Response 429 is not retryable under current code; Request 429 is.
- `with_credential_owner/2` enriches Request authentication failures and recursively Stream/failed wrappers. It has no Response-authentication or request-transformer enrichment clause. Do not generate transformer tags for an enrichment-invariance claim; those inputs are intentionally outside the supported wrapper set in this plan.
- `public_reason_for/1` passes through any atom, despite its doc's “allowlisted” wording. Do not assert a universal finite allowlist over arbitrary atoms. This is existing contract/documentation tension, not an unreachable branch, and requires separate coordinator review if changed.
- A Stream wrapper can contain arbitrary causes for recovery and public-reason delegation; `from_reason/2` only explicitly unwraps Streams with a Request cause. Do not claim all public methods share identical wrapper behavior.
- >=500 guards accept integer values above standard HTTP range. No production guard changes or unsupported HTTP validity invariant are part of this plan.

## Coordinator-only validation commands and acceptance

No commands below were run during planning. Execute after merged-plan implementation, from the authorized checkout using its existing isolated test DB configuration. Route logs through working Context Mode; its current disk-I/O failure is a validation-tooling blocker to resolve, not permission to claim a pass.

1. Issue quality check: `mix q` (includes formatting; no separate format invocation). Because this is a dirty tree and the alias also includes `deps.unlock --unused`, coordinator must review resulting changes and preserve unrelated user work.
2. Isolated owning suite: `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/zaq/agent/error_message_test.exs`.
3. Only when diagnosing a property failure, reproduce with the reported seed: `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/zaq/agent/error_message_test.exs --seed <reported-seed>`. Do not add repeated seed runs without a failure or unresolved concern.
4. Fresh focused coverage: `MIX_ENV=test mix coveralls.json test/zaq/agent/error_message_test.exs --output-dir cover/error-message-coverage` with 600,000 ms timeout. Inspect the full `lib/zaq/agent/error_message.ex` entry in that new JSON, not aggregate repository percentage. The initial 81% is user-supplied and was not remeasured. Any report from a failed/timed-out command is not acceptance evidence.
5. Coordinator performs merged-scope/full fresh coverage per its lifecycle (`mix coveralls.json`, then `mix coverup` only after successful generation), and final `mix precommit` with 900,000 ms timeout when the combined work is ready for final approval. Do not repeat a full test run redundantly at the final gate.

Acceptance: all existing and new owning-file tests/properties pass without relaxed assertions; every supplied line's clause is executed; both ownership case arms and the status/provenance boundaries are explicitly verified; public output contains only the exact safe messages/atoms/maps asserted; no production or shared-state seams were introduced. Target whole-module coverage >=95% per handbook, recording remaining uncovered behavior and justified exceptions rather than excluding lines. If the supplied line set is incomplete relative to fresh whole-module coverage, report the additional gaps to the coordinator for merged-scope handling.

E2E is unnecessary: this change tests deterministic translation contracts with no new UI journey or integration behavior. No browser authoring or execution is part of this module's validation plan. Tracking, final validation, and Git actions remain coordinator-owned.


Coordinator execution override: tests only in assigned files, preserve pre-existing edits; no worker Mix/Git/Beadwork mutations. Coordinator alone runs mix q and added/edited tests --cover. No full-suite or precommit execution for this coverage task.
